themes_detail.label: Unsanitary Conditions Surge
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary condition complaints spiked to 116 last week—more than double the 8-week average of 53.9 complaints per week—representing a 115% increase (z-score: 6.53) in what appears to be a THIS WEEK acceleration, suggesting a potential public health or sanitation service crisis in Crown Heights.
evidence: 116 unsanitary condition complaints last week vs. 53.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (115% spike, z-score 6.53)
This represents the sharpest single-week acceleration among all reported spikes
Aligns with recurring community board budget requests for expanded outreach and facilities improvements, suggesting chronic underlying infrastructure gaps
reporting_angles: Ground-level canvass: What specific blocks or addresses are generating complaints? Interview residents about conditions and SanDep response times.
Systemic angle: Has the city reduced sanitation worker staffing or collection frequency recently? Cross-check with DSNY data.
Service equity: Is this spike concentrated in specific blocks or business corridors, and does it correlate with recent commercial activity (e.g., outdoor dining reopenings)?

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Code Violations Exploding
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints surged to 3 last week from a near-zero 8-week average of 0.1 per week (2,300% spike, z-score: 8.69), indicating potential widespread non-compliance with dining regulations or rapid unmanaged expansion of street sheds in Crown Heights THIS WEEK.
evidence: 3 outdoor dining complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average (2,300% increase, z-score 8.69, severity: high)
This is the single largest percentage spike across all 311 complaint categories
Timing coincides with broader NYC reopening/warmer weather patterns; may signal compliance monitoring gap or shed proliferation
reporting_angles: What are the specific violations? Inspect complaint records for location data and violation types (unpermitted sheds, blocking sidewalks, etc.)
Interview NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) to understand if Crown Heights has been flagged for compliance issues or if inspections have ramped up.
Business impact: Talk to restaurant owners on Nostrand Ave or Franklin Ave corridors about permitting challenges and shed costs.

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Defacement Wave
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints jumped to 12 last week from a 2.4 weekly baseline (405% spike, z-score: 4.68), suggesting a coordinated tagging campaign or reactive uptick in community reporting of this week's visible vandalism across Crown Heights.
evidence: 12 graffiti complaints last week vs. 2.4 weekly average (405% spike, z-score 4.68)
Represents the third-largest percentage spike in this week's data
Potential convergence signal: May overlap with unsanitary condition complaints if complaints focus on same blocks
reporting_angles: Spot-check: Walk key corridors (Nostrand, Franklin, Atlantic) and photograph current graffiti to map the problem geographically.
Interview Parks Dept and NYPD about response protocols and whether tagging crews are active in the area.
Community perception: Interview long-term residents on whether graffiti has worsened or if complaint reporting behavior has shifted.

themes_detail.label: Dangling Street Sign Hazard
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints spiked to 7 about 3 weeks ago from a 0.8 weekly average (833% spike, z-score: 7.54), indicating a potential infrastructure maintenance backlog or storm-related damage creating public safety hazards in Crown Heights.
evidence: 7 street sign complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average (833% spike, z-score 7.54)
Timing suggests potential weather event (heavy winds/storm) or broader deferred maintenance issue
Falls outside the immediate 1-week window but remains statistically significant and unresolved
reporting_angles: NYPD or DOT: Request data on which streets have reported dangling/missing signs and timeline for repairs.
Safety angle: Document any incidents or near-misses involving pedestrians or vehicles and signs; interview residents in affected blocks.
Systemic angle: Does this align with DOT or NYC budget cuts to street infrastructure maintenance? Cross-reference with capital budget data.

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge Complaints
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle (Uber/Lyft) complaints jumped to 18 last week from a 6.4 weekly baseline (182% spike, z-score: 4.25), suggesting increased traffic congestion, illegal parking, or driver behavior issues tied to ride-hailing services in Crown Heights THIS WEEK.
evidence: 18 for-hire vehicle complaints last week vs. 6.4 weekly average (182% spike, z-score 4.25)
Aligns with long-standing illegal parking complaints (2,156 total over 90 days), suggesting overlap in root causes
May correlate with outdoor dining expansion (both suggest street congestion and sidewalk interference)
reporting_angles: Data dive: Cross-tabulate for-hire vehicle complaints with illegal parking and outdoor dining complaints to identify overlap blocks.
Interview TLC (Taxi and Limousine Commission): Are there compliance issues specific to Crown Heights, or is this borough-wide?
Resident experience: Talk to shop owners and residents on busy commercial blocks (Nostrand, Franklin) about congestion and safety impacts.
